$comment: Known environment misconfigurations that the compatibility graph doesn't model (they're not a version mismatch, they're a broken permission/env-var/ABI assumption). Each entry is matched against raw log text (e.g. `rocminfo`/`rocm-smi` stderr, or a pasted error) by substring/regex. Researched and sourced 2026-09-05 from real GitHub issues.

issues.symptom: `rocminfo` (or any ROCm tool) fails immediately with a permission error, even though the GPU and driver are otherwise fine.
issues.cause: On most distros, `/dev/kfd` is owned by the `render` group (older docs/packages sometimes only mention `video`). If the current user isn't a member of that group, every ROCm tool fails at the same first step.
issues.fix: sudo usermod -aG render,video $LOGNAME   # then log out and back in (or reboot) for the group change to take effect

issues.symptom: A consumer Radeon GPU (e.g. RX 6600/6600 XT, gfx1032) isn't in ROCm's officially supported list, so `rocminfo`/PyTorch don't recognize it even though it's in the same architecture family as a supported card.
issues.cause: ROCm gates support by exact gfx target. Cards in the same family as a supported one (e.g. gfx1032 vs. supported gfx1030) can often be forced to work by overriding the reported ISA version, at the cost of running an untested configuration.
issues.fix: export HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0   # maps gfx1032 -> gfx1030; adjust the target version to the nearest *supported* gfx in the same family
issues.caveats: Does not work on Windows ROCm builds (the override is a no-op there). On gfx1031/gfx1032 specifically, ROCm 6.4.3+ and the 7.2.x line have shipped builds where this override loads the model but then segfaults on the first prompt, with no confirmed fix as of this research date -- treat as 'may not work', not a guaranteed fix.
issues.severity_note: workaround, not a real fix -- unsupported configuration

issues.symptom: A library that inspects `torch.version.hip` to detect the ROCm ABI (bitsandbytes, ComfyUI, and others do this) misdetects the version or crashes after upgrading to a build from AMD's newer TheRock build system.
issues.cause: TheRock's build changed the format of `torch.version.hip` (e.g. from a `7.2.x`-style string to `7.13.x`-style), which breaks any downstream code that parses it expecting the old format. This is an active upstream regression, not something the user misconfigured.
issues.fix: No user-side fix -- pin the previously-working torch build for the affected library until it's updated to read the new `torch.version.hip` format (or `torch.version.rocm`, added as a more stable alternative), or check if the downstream project has already shipped a compatibility patch.
